sections.title: Physics daily — 2026-11-19 announcement batch
sections.text: Ten notable recent papers, ranked by inferred cross-listing and technical relevance. Dominant pattern: cross-field toolbuilding for quantum many-body systems and gravitational-wave/neutron-star physics, plus data-driven methods that expose or measure physical structure. Spoken agenda: neutron-star and LISA modeling, an atomic-superfluid measurement, then quantum algorithms and theory constraints.

sections.title: Nonlinearly Causal General-Relativistic Superfluid Hydrodynamics: Simulating Vortex Dynamics in Neutron-Star Interiors
sections.abstract: The authors formulate causal, strongly hyperbolic general-relativistic superfluid hydrodynamics with vortex forces and line energy, and introduce a stable finite-volume method for simulating vortex dynamics in neutron-star interiors.
sections.claimed_result: The authors derive nonlinear-causality and strong-hyperbolicity conditions, show that commonly used force-balanced models without line tension can be ill-posed at short wavelengths, and report the first multidimensional nonlinear simulations of relativistic superfluid vortex dynamics, including a simplified spin-down calculation.
sections.evidence_type: Computational and theoretical; finite-volume simulations validated against an exact relativistic superfluid Riemann solution and Kelvin-wave dispersion, followed by neutron-star equilibrium and spin-down calculations.
sections.unique_caveat: The neutron-star application uses a simplified, shear-free vortex-array model and prescribed vortex release/repinning; it does not yet model the full microphysics of vortex-lattice elasticity and pinning.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 1.00, composed of four cross-lists; no positive HF/HN attention signal was recorded, and citation data were unavailable. Its placement at the top of that tied tier reflects the concrete, cross-field numerical framework, not measured popularity.

sections.title: SlotFlow-GB: A Neural Framework for Trans-Dimensional Inference of Overlapping Galactic Binaries
sections.abstract: The authors introduce a neural posterior approximation that jointly infers the number and parameters of overlapping Galactic binaries from simulated LISA data without fixing the source count in advance.
sections.claimed_result: On year-long, high-SNR simulations with up to ten binaries in a 2 μHz interval, the inferred source count is within one of the true count in 94% of cases; inference takes 41 ms per band on an NVIDIA GH200 GPU, according to the authors.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; simulated LISA observations and controlled source-overlap evaluations, with likelihood-based refinement tests.
sections.unique_caveat: The study uses a restricted high-SNR simulation regime, up to ten binaries, stationary Gaussian noise, and no unresolved Galactic foreground; source-count probabilities are not fully calibrated and cross-source parameter correlations are not explicitly represented.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 1.00, composed of four cross-lists (tied top signal tier). No positive HF/HN attention signal was recorded; citation data were unavailable. Its high placement reflects unusually broad physics/data-method cross-listing and a testable inference result, not a readership claim.

sections.title: Local velocimetry for atomic superfluids: from Riemann rarefaction waves to quantized vortices
sections.abstract: The authors demonstrate two-dimensional velocity-field imaging in an atomic superfluid by mapping its wavefunction phase gradient to matter-wave interference fringe displacements, then apply it to rarefaction flows and quantized vortices.
sections.claimed_result: The authors use Raman–Bragg matter-wave interferometry to observe self-similar 1D Riemann rarefaction flow and map the 2D velocity field around quantized vortices, including quantized circulation.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; interferometric measurements in a two-dimensional ultracold atomic superfluid.
sections.unique_caveat: Fringe-phase calibration and interaction-induced phase shifts affect the velocity readout; the supplementary material discusses calibration and an approximately 10% correction associated with finite-duration spin-transfer pulses.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.75, from three cross-lists; no positive HF/HN attention signal was recorded; citation data were unavailable. It ranks above other papers in this signal tier because it reports an experimental measurement method and direct demonstrations rather than only a proposed capability.

sections.title: High-Accuracy Neural-Network Quantum States via Randomized Real-Time Dynamics
sections.abstract: The authors propose dynamical averaging, which uses randomized real-time evolution to reduce errors in neural-network quantum-state estimates of ground-state observables without additional energy minimization or model complexity.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove up-to-quadratic suppression of errors in arbitrary ground-state observables and report accelerated convergence with lower observable errors in non-integrable spin-model demonstrations.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical and computational; proof plus numerical tests on non-integrable spin models.
sections.unique_caveat: The numerical demonstration is on the tested spin models; the abstract does not establish performance across other Hamiltonian families or report a universal empirical error reduction.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.75, from three cross-lists; no positive HF/HN attention signal was recorded; citation data were unavailable. The result combines a general error-suppression argument with tests on non-integrable spin models.

sections.title: Who Moved My $Z$ Boson? Revealing Resonance Features Inside a Neural Network
sections.abstract: The authors identify internal features corresponding to particle resonances in a generative collider model trained on real LHC data, and show that manipulating a selected feature changes the generated Z-boson mass peak.
sections.claimed_result: In ShellFlow, the authors report learned features representing the Z, J/ψ, and Υ resonances; altering or removing the Z feature changes its generated mass/peak width while leaving most of the rest of the invariant-mass spectrum largely unchanged.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; mechanistic analysis of a generative model trained on real LHC data.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an intervention on a model representation, not a new measurement of the Z boson; the conclusion is specific to the trained generator and its feature-selection analysis.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.75, from three cross-lists; no positive HF/HN attention signal was recorded; citation data were unavailable. The placement reflects the concrete model-intervention result and its bridge between collider physics and interpretability methods.

sections.title: UV Bounds on Inflationary Parity Violation
sections.abstract: The authors analyze whether ultraviolet-complete models can generate detectable parity violation in inflationary correlators, finding that existing tensor-scalar-scalar bispectrum bounds strongly constrain that possibility.
sections.claimed_result: For tensor-to-scalar ratios near current observational limits, the authors find detectable parity-odd trispectrum signals incompatible with or close to the validity boundary of the examined UV completions; smaller ratios remain possible only with a very large TSS vertex enhancement.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical; analysis of effective-field-theory bounds in fermionic and string-theoretic examples.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is conditional on the UV completions and parameter regimes examined; it does not rule out every mechanism for cosmological parity violation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.75, from three cross-lists; no positive HF/HN attention signal was recorded; citation data were unavailable. The paper connects high-energy effective-theory consistency to a potentially observable cosmological signal.

sections.title: Evolving Decoding Algorithms for Quantum Error Correction
sections.abstract: The authors encode published belief-propagation decoders in a domain-specific language and use grammatical evolution to search for faster, more accurate decoders for quantum low-density parity-check codes.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report an evolved decoder with 23% fewer logical errors than a damped BP+OSD-0 baseline at 0.64 times its runtime, and faster-than-reference decoders across tested noise levels and code settings.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; decoder benchmarks on quantum LDPC-code simulations. The arXiv comment states acceptance at the NeurIPS 2026 EvoRobust Workshop.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported comparisons are benchmark results for the tested codes, noise models, and decoder implementations; the paper does not report deployment on a live quantum processor.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.75, from three cross-lists; no positive HF/HN attention signal was recorded; citation data were unavailable. Its evidence includes a checkable time/error trade-off and an accepted-workshop comment, alongside the cross-listing.

sections.title: Tunable Ground-State Entanglement in Fully Connected Quantum Systems: From Logarithmic to Volume-Law Scaling
sections.abstract: The authors construct a fully connected qubit Hamiltonian in which changing only the interaction normalization produces rigorously controlled ground-state entanglement ranging from subextensive scaling to a volume law.
sections.claimed_result: For the constructed all-to-all bipartite model, the authors prove entropy scaling Θ(n^(2−2κ) log n) for 1/2 < κ ≤ 1 and Θ(n) at κ = 1/2; a system-size-independent gap is proved for 3/4 ≤ κ ≤ 1.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical, with weak-coupling analysis and numerical calculations for part of the parameter range.
sections.unique_caveat: The gap is rigorously bounded away from zero only for 3/4 ≤ κ ≤ 1; its persistence for 1/2 ≤ κ < 3/4 is suggested by weak-coupling analysis and numerics, not proved in the abstract.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.75, from three cross-lists; no positive HF/HN attention signal was recorded; citation data were unavailable. Its placement within the tier reflects a rigorous asymptotic result spanning quantum information and statistical mechanics.

sections.title: Fast extraction of universal data from temporal spectrum: Applications to Haagerup CFT and monopole scattering
sections.abstract: The authors propose extracting conformal-field-theory spectral data from the transfer matrix of an infinite matrix-product state after short imaginary-time evolution, and apply the method to the Haagerup CFT and monopole scattering.
sections.claimed_result: Applying the method, the authors obtain a charge-resolved Haagerup CFT spectrum to higher levels and central charge c = 2.137(27); they also identify the Maldacena–Ludwig monopole boundary with the ground state of the Fidkowski–Kitaev Hamiltonian after space-time rotation.
sections.evidence_type: Computational and theoretical; infinite matrix-product-state transfer spectra and a proposed field-theory/lattice correspondence.
sections.unique_caveat: The central charge is a numerical extraction; the abstract does not give a systematic-error budget beyond the quoted uncertainty or establish convergence across independent methods.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.75, from three cross-lists; no positive HF/HN attention signal was recorded; citation data were unavailable. Its placement reflects the cross-field method and the reported numerical CFT estimate, not external readership.

sections.title: Certified Discovery of Quantum Phase Diagrams
sections.abstract: The authors give quantum and classical algorithms for mapping phase diagrams of smooth families of local Hamiltonians, with verifiable certificates for reported transitions under stated reference-state assumptions.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove a polynomial-time quantum algorithm at inverse-polynomial gap resolution and provide a quasipolynomial-time classical algorithm at constant gap resolution; numerical experiments test phase structures in several model systems.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical and computational; algorithmic proof with numerical experiments on model quantum systems.
sections.unique_caveat: Success assumes at least one correct reference-ground-state preparation in every gapped region; the algorithms also depend on gap-resolution and smooth-family assumptions and do not remove those input requirements.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.75, from three cross-lists; no positive HF/HN attention signal was recorded; citation data were unavailable. It sits in the same tier as other three-cross-list candidates; selection reflects the verifiable transition-certificate claim and numerical model demonstrations.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.text: Quantum many-body methods span measurement, inference, and mathematical guarantees: local superfluid velocimetry (2611.26608), neural quantum-state observables (2611.26587), entanglement scaling (2611.26430), CFT transfer spectra (2611.26257), and certified phase diagrams (2611.25064). Gravitational-wave work spans overlapping Galactic-binary inference for LISA simulations (2611.26057) and neutron-star vortex hydrodynamics (2611.26547), distinct analysis and simulation efforts rather than observational confirmation. Machine learning supports LISA inference, quantum-state estimates, and QEC decoding (2611.25880), while the collider paper (2611.26291) probes internal resonance features of a data-trained generator. UV consistency bounds on inflationary parity (2611.26594) and hyperbolicity constraints for relativistic superfluids (2611.26547) link formal theory with possible physical observables.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.text: Author-stated limitations and synthesis directions: (1) SlotFlow-GB source-count calibration and omitted cross-binary correlations, high-SNR/no-foreground validation (2611.26057) suggest testing joint posteriors with lower SNR, foregrounds, gaps, glitches, and time-varying noise. (2) The neutron-star model omits vortex-lattice shear and prescribes release/repinning (2611.26547); include elastic modes and microphysical pinning laws. (3) Atomic-superfluid velocimetry depends on phase calibration and interaction/finite-pulse corrections (2611.26608); quantify systematics across regimes and cross-calibrate independently. (4) The uniform entanglement gap is proved only for 3/4 ≤ κ ≤ 1 (2611.26430); prove or disprove persistence at lower κ. (5) Certified phase-diagram discovery assumes correct reference states in each gapped region (2611.25064); test certificate reliability under state errors and small gaps.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.text: The strongest shared signal is methodological: better ways to measure, infer, or simulate difficult physical structure. With no recorded external attention and unavailable Semantic Scholar data, this is a cross-listing-led selection of notable work, not a defensible measure of what was most read or discussed.
